objective: Prove that re-routing a network at any set of contacts (exchanging how its two rings continue there, the partial duality of maps) keeps the contact graph and so every contact's persistence; that re-routing a square, triangular or honeycomb torus along whole classes of contacts gives networks of lines that read their distance plainly at every size; and that on the square contact graph every small ring is late, so a re-routed square torus that reads its distance plainly has only rings of linear size.
status: Proved 2026-11-09: re-routing a network at any set of contacts (Chmutov's partial duality) keeps every arc of the contact graph and so every contact's persistence; the line network of the n x n square torus (2n staircase rings, ring graph a cycle) keeps every contact persistent and reads its distance plainly by single fastest ways at every size (triangular and honeycomb lines computed to n = 20); and on the square contact graph a ring inside a box of side 2^k - 2 is late, so an on-time re-routing of the n x n torus (n >= 64) has at most 64n rings of at least n/8 - 4 contacts: lines, not a plane of rings.
title: Re-routing keeps persistence, and the plain reading needs long rings
